title: Amber and oud soy candle
subtitle: A dark, resinous soy wax jar candle
excerpt: A dark, smoky soy wax jar candle fragranced with amber and oud fragrance oils at 7% of wax weight. Amber provides a resinous, vanilla-tinged warmth; oud adds a dry, smoky woody depth. Pour into a 200 ml glass jar and cure for five to seven days before lighting.
sourceNotes: Fragrance oil flash points: amber fragrance oil typically >100°C, oud fragrance oil typically >80°C (supplier SDS, Bramble Berry 2023). Both are safe to add at the 65°C pour temperature for container soy wax. 7% combined fragrance load is within the safe range for container soy candles (maximum load typically 10% by weight).

recipe.batchNotes: Pour multiple jars from a single melt. Keep the 7% fragrance load consistent.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure five to seven days before the first burn. Amber and oud are base notes and develop depth during the cure.
recipe.temperatureNote: Pour at 60 to 65°C. Amber and oud fragrance oils are low-volatility, high-flashpoint oils; there is no risk of flash at this temperature.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool, dry cupboard out of direct sunlight. Fragrance fades after about 18 months; the candle remains usable.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which a fragrance oil can ignite if exposed to a flame. Amber and oud fragrance oils have high flash points and are safe to add at 65°C.
The first burn of a jar candle, which sets the melt pool. Burning until the top surface has fully liquefied prevents tunnelling on subsequent burns.
The resting period after pouring, during which fragrance oil bonds with the wax matrix. Five to seven days produces the best scent throw.

content.text: Warm the glass jar briefly. Stick the wick tab to the base of the jar and hold in place with the centring bar across the rim.

Melt the soy wax in the pouring pitcher over a water bath or low heat to 75°C. Cool to 65°C. Add both fragrance oils and stir for 30 seconds. Pour into the prepared jar in one steady pour. Do not move the jar until fully set.
Trim the wick to 6 mm after 24 hours. Cure for five to seven days before lighting.
